title: Aesthetics at Home (Module 6A, lesson 31)
summary: Cleaning includes putting things in a decided place; otherwise you waste time finding things and become unorganised. A cluttered house with unmatching curtains and too many decorations restricts movement; a good home has furniture in proportion to the room, well-arranged objects, curtains that give uniformity, pleasing colours, adequate lighting and free movement, so we feel rested and comfortable. Artistic touch makes things beautiful and comfortable.

Materials: vase (matching the surroundings; a small basket suits cane furniture and coir coverings), a pin holder (iron nails fixed on a heavy metal base, closely spaced, rust-free and long enough to hold stems) or oasis (absorbs a lot of water and keeps flowers moist; soak until bubbles stop; reusable 2–4 times; easier for beginners to balance flowers), fresh or artificial flowers, green leaves and twigs. Odd numbers of flowers (as few as three in ikebana, the Japanese art), of varying sizes. Twigs give a natural look; leaves fill gaps, give a background and make the arrangement resemble nature; wash dirty leaves and trim wilted ones.

Fix the pin holder to the container and pour water to cover it (or soak the oasis); decide the shape (triangle, right angle, oval, S-shape); choose flowers of different sizes; pluck flowers early in the morning and cut under water; cut stems at different lengths with the tallest at least 1½ times the width of the vase; arrange the tallest first and then the others in order of height, placing each branch firmly in the pin holder or oasis; put flowers at different heights with space between them, facing towards you; bigger flowers at the bottom, medium in the centre and buds at the top so it is not top-heavy; fill gaps with leaves of different sizes; hide the pin holder with leaves or stones; place against a contrasting background.

Size in proportion to the room and container (flowers 1½ times the height of the vase); balance (not top-heavy or lopsided); rhythm (the eye should travel easily around, by repeating shape, colour and texture and arranging at different heights); graded sizes from full-bloom to buds; stem ends close together; the plant material more important than the vase; not too many different colours (use small dull flowers with bright ones); emphasise twig shapes with space around each flower; harmony of flowers, leaves and vase.

Rangoli or alpana: traditional floor decoration on doorsteps, courtyards and verandahs with colours, flower petals, rice or maida powder. Tips: select the design to suit the festival or occasion, draw in double lines to fill between, ensure uniformity and balance, use contrasting colours next to each other, use a scale to neaten outlines, fill evenly and press flat, and fill the background so the design looks part of the floor. Coloured sawdust: sieve sawdust, mix 30 g dyeing colour in half a glass of water, dry in shade and store in plastic bags. Accessories: hang paintings according to wall size (a group of small paintings fitted in an imaginary square or rectangle), use spot lights, hang straight and even, harmonise lamp colours with the décor, place cushions randomly for colour, do not crowd curios and group similar materials together.

objective: Priya arranges flowers in a vase. Steps: (i) Fix the pin holder to the container and pour water until it covers the pin holder. (ii) Decide the shape of the arrangement. Missing step 1: ______. Missing step 2: ______ (iii) Cut the stems at different lengths, with the tallest branch 1½ times the width of the vase. (iv) Fill the gaps with leaves. Complete the missing steps.

Missing step 1 (after deciding the shape): choose flowers of different sizes and pluck them in the morning; cut stems under water. Missing step 2: arrange the tallest flower first and then the others in order of height, with bigger flowers at the bottom and buds at the top.
Correct the following. (a) Flowers should be plucked in the evening. (b) An even number of flowers should be chosen. (c) Buds should be placed at the bottom.

vsa: What is the role of twigs and leaves in a flower arrangement?
Twigs give a natural look and enhance the shape of the arrangement. Leaves fill gaps, give a background to flowers and resemble nature.
What is a pin holder? Why is it used?
It is a heavy metal base fitted with closely spaced iron nails. It holds the flower and leaf stems in position in the vase.
State two principles of flower arrangement.
The arrangement should be balanced, neither top-heavy nor lopsided. It should be in proportion to the room and the vase.
Write two points on the importance of arranging things in an orderly manner at home.
Things can be found quickly, saving time and energy. The house looks neat and comfortable and gives a pleasant feeling.
State two tips for making a good rangoli.
Select the design to suit the occasion and draw it in double lines. Use contrasting colours and fill evenly, pressing flat.
sa: Which three points should be kept in mind while hanging paintings on walls?

(i) Hang paintings according to size and space: big paintings on big walls or a group of small ones in an imaginary rectangle. (ii) Use spot lights and hang them straight and even. (iii) Colour of lamps should match the décor and paintings should not be crowded.
Enumerate the principles of flower arrangement (three points).

(i) Size in proportion to the room and vase, and a balanced arrangement. (ii) Rhythm: the eye should travel smoothly, with flowers graded from blooms to buds. (iii) Plant material more important than the vase, with harmony of colours.
Give five suggestions to beautify a room for guests (three of them).

(i) Arrange a flower vase in a corner or side table with an odd number of flowers. (ii) Keep furniture in proportion, adequate lighting and hang paintings straight. (iii) Place cushions and indoor plants and avoid clutter.
Explain how a rangoli is made (three points).

(i) Select the design to suit the occasion and draw it with chalk in double lines. (ii) Fill with colours, flower petals or coloured sawdust using contrasting colours. (iii) Fill evenly, neaten the edges with a scale and fill the background.
la: Explain the steps of making a flower arrangement.

(i) Collect the vase, pin holder or oasis, flowers, leaves and twigs. (ii) Fix the pin holder in the container and cover with water or soak the oasis. (iii) Decide the shape and choose flowers of different sizes. (iv) Cut stems at different lengths with the tallest 1½ times the vase width, and place the tallest first. (v) Put bigger flowers at the bottom, medium in the centre and buds at the top. (vi) Fill the gaps with leaves, hide the holder and place against a contrasting background.
